subject: Order form: collection playbook, commit phasing and VAT evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@pulsehealth.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sage Holdings Procurement <procurement@sageholdings.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify collection lane + VAT evidence for order form

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to confirm two things before we share the order form with finance: 1) how collection will be handled if we phase the minimum commit across Q1/Q2 (they want the ledger line split by tranche), and 2) what evidence you need for PulseHealth's VAT registration to avoid withholding.

Attached is our copy of the order form with small annotations. Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will issue separate invoices per tranche or one consolidated invoice with allocation lines (they prefer separate invoices per tranche)
- If Redwood needs the full VAT certificate or a country tax ID + confirmation email from our accounting vendor

If you can loop in legal for any redline suggestions (MSA cross-ref), that would help speed procurement. Looking to get exec approval this week.

Jordan
Head of Procurement
PulseHealth
Attachments: PulseHealth_Redlined_OrderForm_v3.docx (annotations)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify collection lane + VAT evidence for order form

Hi Jordan —

Thanks — this is straightforward to resolve. Quick answers up front:
- We can support separate invoices per tranche (preferred by you) and will mark each invoice with tranche identifiers and billing period to satisfy your ledger.
- For EU VAT we generally need a PDF of the VAT registration (certificate) and a company tax ID. In some AP jurisdictions a confirmation email from your vendor is acceptable; let me confirm specifically for PulseHealth's country.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share a short collection playbook (internal ops + what will appear on the invoice) and a sample invoice line layout so procurement can validate the ledger mapping.
2) I’ll ask Kimberly/legal to review the order form redlines for any MSA cross-references (billing address, tax gross-up, and remit entity).
3) If procurement wants DocuSign sequencing per-tranche, we can set that up.

Looping Kimberly and Ben here for legal and billing ops input.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo / Jordan — adding legal perspective.

I reviewed the redlined order form and have three asks before we finalize:
1) Billing entity: if PulseHealth is paying from a UK entity but VAT registered elsewhere, we need a remit-entity clause in the order form to avoid downstream tax exposure. Suggest inserting: "Invoices will be issued to the remit entity specified in Section X; tax liability remains with the payer unless otherwise agreed in writing."
2) Proration for phased commits: propose a short appendix that defines per-tranche activation and invoicing schedule, with an explicit example table so procurement can reconcile ledger lines.
3) Evidence threshold: accept a VAT certificate PDF or a government portal confirmation link + company tax ID. If procurement can provide the PDF it’s the cleanest path.

I am attaching a tracked-change draft of the order form (PulseHealth_Redlined_OrderForm_v3.docx) and a one-pager invoice sample. Ben — can billing ops run the sample invoice through our AR staging to confirm format OK?

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: PulseHealth_Redlined_OrderForm_v3.docx (tracked changes), msa-change-log.txt

Kimberly — I ran the sample invoice through our AR staging. Notes for procurement:
- Separate invoices per tranche: AR can emit distinct invoice numbers and include a "Tranche" custom field. That will let your accounting map each ledger line to the correct commitment.
- We can include an appendix line showing allocation percent and token counts for each tranche.
- If PulseHealth prefers one consolidated invoice with allocation lines, we can do that too, but it will require an internal mapping step for your accounting system.

Jordan — attached is a PDF of the sample invoice layout (we'll send as native PDF with each invoice). If you confirm you want separate invoices per tranche, we will: (a) include tranche ID on every invoice, (b) generate invoices on the activation date for each tranche, and (c) provide a CSV export of invoices for your ledger.

Ben
Billing Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
